### Step by step
1) Position → knee **60°**, hip **abducted + ER**, foot on the other shin
2) Incision → **curved**, **2 cm above** the **adductor tubercle**, ≈**3 cm medial** to the patella → **6 cm below** the joint line (Hoppenfeld)

[[FIG: Fig 7B.13, 7B.14 · 7B.03

| Door | Route | Reaches |
|---|---|---|
| **In front** of the sMCL | Medial parapatellar arthrotomy | Front of the joint |
| **Behind** the sMCL | Between **medial gastrocnemius and semimembranosus** → peel gastrocnemius off the capsule | **Posteromedial corner**  |
[[FIG: Fig 7B.15, 7B.16 · 7B.03

### Dangers
- **Saphenous nerve + long saphenous vein** → come out between **gracilis and sartorius**
- **Inferior medial genicular artery** → round the upper tibia, deep to the sMCL → torn lifting medial gastrocnemius off the capsule → bleeds only after **tourniquet** release (Hoppenfeld)
- **Popliteal artery** → on the posterior capsule beside medial gastrocnemius
- **Big flaps** → **haematoma → skin necrosis** → drain

7B.08.b:
HIGH YIELD
- Round the knee → **no true plane** in most approaches → safe because the nerves are **behind**
- The true planes are on the **lateral side** → ITB / biceps, vastus lateralis / biceps, and in the leg **peronei vs the back muscles**
- Medial gastrocnemius / semimembranosus → both tibial → **safe**, not true

- **Over-the-top distal femur** → vastus lateralis / biceps → femoral / sciatic
